helpmed0g: Valentin Helpmed joined the replacements on Day 4. An old hand checked his pack straps before asking his name.

Valentin Helpmed cleaned grit from the rifle bolt with a scrap of cloth. The scrap was once the clean part of a shirt. A letter from home found Valentin Helpmed before the night shift. Valentin Helpmed folded it small and kept it close. Valentin Helpmed left the work of a rifleman to become a stretcher bearer. Someone from the old section came over to see how it was going.

A shell landed close to S-F21. When the dust settled Valentin Helpmed was still there, holding his mother's thimble, laughing without sound. A letter from home found Valentin Helpmed before the night shift. Valentin Helpmed folded it small and kept it close.
leo.glc: Isidor Glc told the sergeant he was a postman. The sergeant said the war needed one of those like it needed more rain, and put him on sentry.
Volunteer number 61. The quartermaster pinned the First Wave ribbon on Isidor Glc's tunic and said: 'Don't let the mud have it.'
Isidor Glc fired at a movement across the wire at S-F13. The man went down: Florian "Shadow" Slightlyreta, grazed.
Rafael "Button" Superfeisty and Isidor Glc made a pact on sentry tonight: whoever gets home first visits the other's family. They shook on it with frozen hands.
Isidor Glc carried three men out of S-F13 on a stretcher. One of them thanked him. Two could not. Victory at Verdel Ridge. Isidor Glc let himself talk about leave for the first time in days.
Isidor Glc and Quentin Adams tried to invent a new card game. The rules only made sense once they stopped betting tobacco.
The men have learned that Isidor Glc counts everything: steps, shells, stars. Tonight it made them laugh, which was worth a great deal.

Isidor Glc drew the street leading to Millbank. There was no room left for the last house, so he turned the page over. A letter from home found Isidor Glc before the night shift. Isidor Glc folded it small and kept it close.
olie300: Arno Olie introduced himself as a bookbinder from Ashford Vale. The corporal repeated the name correctly. That helped more than the advice.
Edmund Callmequeeno and Arno Olie sat through a quiet hour without finding anything to say. At relief, the next watch was told it had been a good hour.

Arno Olie heard a man laugh beyond the enemy parapet. The sound was ordinary enough to be more unsettling than a shot. Word came down the line: Verdel Ridge is ours. Arno Olie shook hands with a corporal he had never spoken to. Today, everyone was a friend.
Arno Olie found water collecting beneath the gun's cover. He sketched a small shelter and took the drawing to the stores.

Arno Olie read a letter saying the neighbor had married again. The whole dugout wanted the first half of the story, which was missing. A letter from home reached Arno Olie before dusk. Arno Olie read it twice and slept a little easier.
Arno Olie fired twice at the enemy post. The second shot found Quentin "Spark" Josiascouper, grazed. Nobody nearby said anything.
zanetaylor_8: Quentin Zanetaylor was a coal miner in Marrow Fen until the posters went up. He came to R-S8 with a tin of tobacco, and within a day the whole squad knew that he counts everything: steps, shells, stars.
Quentin Zanetaylor was peppered by shell splinters at R-S8. A medic picked them out one by one while the next salvo came in.
